title: Microwindow mosaic checklist and rollout digest
content:
Summary:
This doc is a working draft for the microwindow rollout we discussed in last week's release sync. Purpose is to capture a compact preflight checklist, a 7-day micro-schedule (hourly guidance for the microwindow), quick decision gates, observability targets, and a first-pass release-notes draft to share with product for review.

Context and goals:
- Target: land traffic-shift for the new batching optimizer into production for a narrow microwindow (2 hours) on 2028-03-20 UTC.
- Why microwindow: validate latency/cost improvements in production without broad exposure; allow rapid rollback on customer-impact signals.
- Success signals: p50 latency within 5% of baseline, p95 <= baseline + 25ms, no increase in error-rate > 0.5% absolute, and stable token-cost metrics (expected -6% per-token).
- Primary constraints: shared GPU pools (Dedicated), region-aware routing; only route 5% of total traffic initially.

Quick owner map:
- Release lead: Lina Chen (owners: runbook and comms)
- Routing & capacity: Tomás Rivera (traffic shift scripts, throttle curves)
- Telemetry & alerting: Aisha Patel (dashboards, sampling)
- Rollback hotfix: Marcus O'Neill (hotpatch PRs, fast rollback)
- Customer comms (CS): Priya Singh (standby)

7-day micro-schedule (high level):
- D-7: Finalize smoke test prompts, remind SRE on standby, tag canaries in CI. (TODO: attach smoke prompt file)
- D-3: Run synthetic load sim against staging with same sequence length distribution; collect p95 baseline.
- D-2: Canary in staging -> brief postmortem, address any kernel mismatches.
- D-1: Deployment frozen for feature branch; preflight checklist below executed by release lead + telemetry.
- Day-of (window starts 12:00 UTC): 11:00 - run final smoke; 11:30 - cut maintenance notice to internal channels; 11:45 - scale up canary capacity; 12:00 - shift 0.5% traffic and monitor for 15m; 12:15 - if green, 5% for 30m; 12:45 - if green, 12% for 30m; 13:15 - if green, hold and evaluate; 13:30 - expand to 50% for 30m; 14:00 - full release or rollback.
- D+1: Post-release triage, collect anomalies, optional small hotfix window.

Preflight checklist (must be green before D-1 freeze):
- CI green for release branch and hotpatch path (PR links in linked_artifacts).
- Telemetry: latency, error-rate, cost-per-token dashboards created and pinned.
- Alerts: temporary guardrails created with low thresholds (p95, 5xx spike, token-cost drift).
- Rollback playbook validated on staging; rollback PR ready to apply with 1-click.
- Capacity: Dedicated pool reservations confirmed for bump (capacity ticket #RES-158).
- Comms: Slack channel #release-microwindow created and all on-call added.
- Stakeholders pinged: SRE, infra, product, CS.

Day-of checklist (operator runbook):
- T-60min: confirm observability feeds live (trace sampling, synthetic checks).
- T-45min: enable elevated logging for canary instances (sampling to 1%).
- T-30min: final sanity run of smoke prompts against canary.
- T-15min: mark runbook as ‘armed’ and notify stakeholders.
- T0: execute traffic ship (use route-shift CLI v2.1).
- Monitor cadence: 5m, 15m, 30m evaluate; use the signal checklist below.
- If any critical alert fires (see gating rules) -> escalate to on-call and immediately shift all canary traffic to fallback model variant; if persistent -> rollback.

Gating rules and decision matrix (abbreviated):
- Immediate abort (shift back to baseline and call bridge) if: error-rate increase > 0.8% absolute, p95 > baseline + 50ms, any customer-facing 5xx spike > 1%
- Soft abort (pause expansion, investigate) if: error-rate increase between 0.3%–0.8%, p95 between +25–50ms, token-cost drift > +10%
- Proceed if: all metrics within success signals for two consecutive windows (15m checks) and no manual complaints reported.

Rollback steps (fast path):
- Executor: Release lead or assigned runbook operator.
- Steps: 1) run `route-shift revert --release microwindow-2028-03` (pre-baked script), 2) confirm traffic returned to baseline, 3) comment on PR and ping on-call, 4) open incident doc if rollback due to errors, 5) schedule hotpatch if needed.

Telemetry & samples to watch (initial sample list):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (all regions, per-model)
- 5xx error-rate and 4xx anomalies
- Token cost per request + aggregate token consumption (per-minute)
- Model-specific outputs: hallucination score sampling (eval harness)
- Queue depth and batch sizes reported by runtime
- Traces for end-to-end request (sampling at 0.5% after release)

Release notes — working draft (to hand to product):
- Feature: Batching optimizer (v1) — reduces per-token GPU utilization by ~6% in canary; expected to improve throughput.
- User-visible impact: none on API surface; slight latency improvement for long-context requests.
- Rollout plan: staged microwindow on 2028-03-20; initial 5% traffic, progressive ramp to 50% during window; full roll after 24h validation.
- Known limitations: may increase p95 for very short requests (<8 tokens) due to batching alignment; we have a guardrail to route those to the existing path until further tuning.
- If anything goes wrong: see rollback matrix in runbook; contact CS for customer-facing note.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need to verify KMS integration for wavefront logs in Private deployments — Aisha to confirm by D-2.
- Should we add an automated canary reroute if error-rate spikes for three consecutive 1m buckets? (Tomás proposal)
- Check whether Dedicated pool autoscaler will preempt competing jobs during the 12:00 window — file ticket with infra.
- Add a short snippet to PR description showing non-regression on small token workloads (N=1000).

Postmortem template (if rollback):
- Timeline (per minute), root cause hypothesis, signal artifacts (dashboards, traces), corrective actions, preventive actions, stakeholders notified, customer impact statement.

Appendix: quick commands and links:
- route-shift CLI usage: `route-shift --release NAME --to-percent 5`
- rollback CLI: `route-shift revert --release NAME`
- Staging replay job: `tools/replay --suite microwindow-smoke --target staging`
- Stash of smoke prompts: CONFLUENCE link above.

Endnotes: This is a working document — expect frequent small edits. Please comment in-line for any gating thresholds you want to tighten. If you prefer a more conservative expansion cadence (e.g., 5% -> 10% -> 25%), say so here.

---
Quick audit trail (edits):
- 2028-03-10 Lina Chen: created base schedule and checklist.
- 2028-03-12 Tomás Rivera: added gating thresholds and traffic cadence.
- 2028-03-14 Aisha Patel: added telemetry items and alerts.
- 2028-03-15 Lina Chen: updated owners and first release notes draft.
